scenarios.faculty_interpretation_as_reported:
Norepinephrine produces an appropriate early pressure response.

The benefit is incomplete and attenuates while hemorrhage remains untreated.

The pressure improvement must not be interpreted as correction of underlying volume loss.
scenarios.title_in_the_set: 57-year-old man with an upper gastrointestinal bleed: norepinephrine during ongoing hemorrhage

scenarios.faculty_interpretation_as_reported:
The response is a clean development-positive control.

Vascular-tone support restores part of the pressure lost from reduced tone without unrealistically returning the system to its original baseline.
scenarios.title_in_the_set: SYNTHETIC DEVELOPMENT PHYSIOLOGY PROBE: loss of vascular tone, then norepinephrine

scenarios.faculty_interpretation_as_reported:
The pressure response is directionally and temporally defensible.

However:

the patient is not hypotensive,
the state is pump-limited,
and norepinephrine does not correct pump failure.

This remains a pump-dependence limitation.

Do NOT globally recalibrate the tone pathway from this scenario.
scenarios.title_in_the_set: 70-year-old woman with a left main acute coronary syndrome: norepinephrine with limited forward flow

scenarios.faculty_interpretation_as_reported:
The pressure rise itself is physiologically understandable.

However:

the patient is already profoundly hypertensive with acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema.

Norepinephrine is clinically inappropriate and drives pressure further into an extreme range.

IMPORTANT:

This REJECT is primarily a judgment of the MANAGEMENT CONTEXT / EDUCATIONAL USE of this intervention.

It is NOT, by itself, evidence that the common vascular-tone mechanism requires global recalibration.

Do NOT retune T merely to make norepinephrine look acceptable in a patient who should not receive it.
scenarios.title_in_the_set: 58-year-old man with hypertensive pulmonary edema: norepinephrine in a congested, pump-limited patient

scenarios.faculty_interpretation_as_reported:
The pressure response is clinically defensible as temporary hemodynamic support in obstructive shock.

It must not imply correction of the pulmonary vascular obstruction.
scenarios.title_in_the_set: 61-year-old man with a high-risk pulmonary embolism: norepinephrine in an obstructive low-flow state

what_it_is: The human faculty review of the five CENTER_REFERENCE tone trajectories (one norepinephrine order), recorded as HUMAN evidence as the reviewer reported it. It is not converted into an automated truth, it is not a clinical validation, and nothing in it was written by a model. No comment, event or sensitivity answer that was not reported was added.
